newsitem.title: USA: Intel to acquire Anite unit.
newsitem.headline: Intel to acquire Anite unit.

text.p: Intel Corp said Thursday it had agreed to acquire Case Technology from Anite Group Plc for $72 million.
Case Tech, based in Copenhagen, is a networking company that specializes in Fast Ethernet networking technology.
Case Tech will become part of Intel's Network Products Division.
The acquisition is subject to approval by Anite shareholders. The companies said they expect a closing by the end of February.
Intel said it plans to make Case Tech part of a new organization called Intel Denmark and to offer all of Case's 146 employees new contracts.
Eric Fullerton, Case Tech managing director, will join Intel's Reinier Tuinzing in managing the Network Systems Operation, Intel said.
Case Tech products will become part of the Intel Network Products Group's offerings, within its strategy of providing a range of networking solutions to manage PC networks.
Case Tech has expertise and products in 10 and 100 Mbps Ethernet switching and small business and branch office routing.
Intel said Case Tech will allow it to significantly increase the volume and range of Fast Ethernet products.

Intel was one of the three original companies that developed and promoted Ethernet as an industry standard for high-bandwidth business solutions. Intel products include EtherExpress PRO/100 adapters, the Express Stackable Hub, the Express Switching Hub, and the recently announced Express 10/100 Fast Ethernet Switch.
